03 Mood and cognition · class card

Cognitive agents

cholinesterase inhibitors · donepezil · rivastigmine · galantamine · memantine

Practice
  1. 76-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease began donepezil 2 weeks ago since then nausea, loose stools, and urinary urgency with leaking pulse 58/min · abdomen soft, active bowel sounds · urinalysis normal → More acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors → donepezil blocks acetylcholinesterase, so acetylcholine builds up and drives gut motility, bladder contraction and vagal slowing of the heart; these effects are often transient and fewer when the dose climbs slowly
  2. 81-year-old man with moderate to severe Alzheimer disease on donepezil a second drug for the dementia was added 3 weeks ago since then dizziness, headache, more confusion and constipation pulse 74/min · moist mouth · pupils normal · bladder not distended → NMDA receptor antagonist → memantine is the drug added to a cholinesterase inhibitor in moderate to severe disease, and dizziness, headache, confusion and constipation are its common effects; his moist mouth, normal pupils and normal pulse argue against a muscarinic antagonist
  3. 79-year-old man with Alzheimer disease, stable on donepezil for a year oxybutynin started 10 days ago for urge incontinence now more forgetful and confused, says his daughter afebrile · dry mouth · pupils 6 mm · urinalysis normal → Anticholinergic effect opposing donepezil → oxybutynin blocks the muscarinic receptors that the extra acetylcholine from donepezil is meant to reach, and anticholinergic drugs bring confusion, dry mouth and wide pupils of their own; urinary incontinence is itself a donepezil effect
